Vi søger nye Managere til vores team.

Det er en fordel, hvis du taler dansk, men som minimum skal du kunne tale flydende engelsk.

Erfaring er selvfølgelig en fordel, men den rigtige personlighed betyder endnu mere for os.

Send gerne en kort besked om dig selv og din erfaring.

 We Are Hiring Restaurant Manager/ waiters 

We are looking for new waiters and waitresses to join our team.

For us, the most important thing is not necessarily years of experience – but having the right attitude and being a kind person.

Speaking Danish is an advantage, but fluent English is required.

We are looking for people who: • Are naturally kind and positive

• Can work well with others without drama or conflicts

• Treat colleagues and customers with respect

• Can stay calm during busy hours

• Take pride in their work

• Feel happy when customers leave happy

• Are responsible and reliable

The atmosphere in our restaurant is very important to us. We want a team that helps each other, respects each other, and works together to give our guests a great experience.

Experience is a plus, but personality and attitude matter even more to us.

Feel free to send us a short message about yourself and your experience.

jobs.employer_name: Impact Fund Denmark (tidl. Investeringsfonden for Udviklingslande)
jobs.description:
Impact Fund Denmark has changed a lot in a short time. We have grown quickly, welcomed many new colleagues and are becoming a larger, more international investment organisation. The same goes for People & Culture and we need and experienced People & Culture professional to strengthen our deliveries in the next phase.

The next phase is about making that growth work well: helping teams come together, strengthening leadership and building and implementing people practices that are robust enough for a more complex organisation without becoming unnecessarily heavy.

 We are looking for a senior People & Culture professional with a proven track record across the full HR agenda, including culture and organisational development. You will bring experience and judgement that strengthen the whole function, with the ambition and potential to be considered for the Head of People & Culture role within three to four years. We also welcome experienced former Heads of People & Culture who want to contribute at this level as an individual contributor.

You will serve the whole organisation, where you will partner closely with senior leaders on organisational, leadership, performance and people questions. You will also take responsibility for selected People & Culture priorities and projects across Impact Fund Denmark.

 You will be a senior sparring partner to the Head of People & Culture and Executive Management, bringing the confidence and experience to challenge established thinking, shape our people strategy and lead its implementation. We expect you to contribute expertise that colleagues across People & Culture, including its leadership, can learn from.

You will report to our Head of People & Culture.

What you’ll be working on

A part of your role will be spent working directly with leaders across our investment organisation. The questions will vary: how a team should be structured, what capabilities we need next, how to address and build performance, how we strengthen succession, or what senior management needs to know before making a people decision.

You will:

• 
lead culture and organisational development initiatives, translating our values and strategic priorities into everyday leadership behaviours, stronger collaboration and clear accountability for performance 

• 
advise senior leaders and Executive Management on organisational, capability, performance and complex people matters across headquarters and regional offices 

• 
prepare analysis, recommendations and decision material for Executive Management and, when relevant, the Board 

• 
support organisational and job design as teams, mandates and responsibilities evolve 

• 
advise on employee relations matters within local employment law and our agreements across headquarters and regional offices 

• 
use people data to identify patterns, challenge assumptions and support better decisions 

• 
take ownership of selected People & Culture projects that cut across the organisation 

• 
work with People Operations, Finance and Legal to ensure that people processes have clear approvals, appropriate controls and traceable documentation, supporting compliance and auditability under the Danish standards on public-sector auditing (SOR) 

• 
work closely with colleagues in Recruitment, People Operations and People Development, and coach and mentor People & Culture colleagues to strengthen their business partnering skills and prepare them for broader responsibilities 

We are currently a relatively lean People & Culture function. That means there is not a specialist team to hand work over to. If a recommendation requires analysis, a presentation, a new process or careful implementation, you should be comfortable taking ownership and doing that work yourself.

What a good first year looks like

After your first year, we would expect that:

• 
Change has moved beyond discussion and design. You have taken ownership of important organisational or capability priorities and helped turn them into practical improvements. 

• 
Core processes work well. Performance, talent and compensation processes in your area are consistent, useful and delivered on time. Leaders can explain and document their decisions, and demonstrate that people resources are used responsibly and effectively in a state-owned organisation. 

• 
Leaders trust your advice and judgement. Senior investment leaders involve you early as a trusted advisor and challenger when important organisational or people questions arise. 

• 
Decisions are better supported. Executive Management receives clear, well-argued recommendations and useful People material from you. 

What we’re looking for

There is no single background that will make someone successful in this role, but you will need substantial experience dealing with the full People & Culture agenda, strategy and policy work, senior stakeholders and an organisation that has really great people and leaders with massive potential.

We would expect you to bring:

• 
substantial experience in a broad senior HR Business Partner, People Partner or People leadership role in international organisations 

• 
experience advising senior executives directly on organisational and people decisions 

• 
demonstrated experience across the full HR agenda, including people strategy, culture and organisational development, recruitment, leadership development, performance, talent and succession, reward, employee relations and HR governance 

• 
practical experience with organisational design and complex employee matters 

• 
strong analytical skills and an ability to turn complicated information into a clear point of view and useful recommendations 

• 
evidence that you can take work from diagnosis through to implementation rather than relying on large specialist teams 

• 
solid knowledge of Danish employment law and HR practice; knowledge of local employment law across our regional offices is considered an advantage 

• 
professional fluency in Danish and English 

It would be useful, but is not essential, if you also have experience with one or more of the following:

• 
financial services, investment or another complex, knowledge-intensive organisation. 

• 
working with Executive teams and Boards or preparing material for Executives and Board discussions 

• 
international HR 

• 
a lean or smaller organisation where senior People professionals remain in delivery 

• 
compensation, People Analytics, talent or succession 

Where the role sits

This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports.

You will be the main People & Culture partner for our investment organisation, working directly with senior investment leaders. At the same time, you will own selected priorities that matter across Impact Fund Denmark and work closely with the Head of People & Culture.

The role will suit someone who likes that combination: being in the room for senior discussions, then staying close enough to the work to make sure something actually happens afterwards.

You should be comfortable moving between an Executive Management discussion, detailed analysis and the practical conversations needed to implement a decision.

Why join Impact Fund Denmark?

You will have close access to the Head of People & Culture and senior leaders across our organisation. You will have considerable scope to influence how we organise, lead and develop our people as Impact Fund Denmark grows and consolidates.

You will also be joining at a point where the organisation is evolving. We are building the people foundation for a larger and more professional international investor, which means some things are already well established while others still need to be shaped.

And the organisation's purpose is tangible. Our investments support green energy and infrastructure, financial services, sustainable food systems and healthcare in developing countries.

Practical details

• 
Location: Østbanegade 135, 2100 Copenhagen Ø 

• 
Position: Permanent, full-time, 39 hours per week including lunch 

• 
Hybrid working: We currently have up to 20% of working time from home starting after 6 months of employment. We believe being in office is important for successful onboarding and integration into team and organisation. 

• 
Application deadline: 23 September 2026

• 
Please apply through our talent platform. Applications submitted outside the platform will not be considered. 

• 
We review applications on an ongoing basis. 

About Impact Fund Denmark

Impact Fund Denmark (IFU – the Investment Fund for Developing Countries) is a Danish impact investor contributing to green, just and inclusive societies as well as supporting the Sustainable Development Goals. Impact Fund Denmark provides risk capital to companies operating in developing countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and parts of Europe. Investments are made on commercial terms in the form of equity, loans and guarantees. Impact Fund Denmark has co-invested in over 1,300 companies in more than 100 developing countries and emerging markets. Contracted investments total EUR 31 billion, of which Impact Fund Denmark has contributed EUR 3.4 billion. Capital under management will be growing from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 5.0 billion over the next few years. Read more at Impact Fund Denmark

jobs.employer_name: Impact Fund Denmark (tidl. Investeringsfonden for Udviklingslande)
jobs.description:
Impact Fund Denmark has grown over the past few years, and many of our colleagues are still relatively new to the organisation. In 2027, our focus is on making that growth work well: strengthening the systems, processes and ways of working a larger organisation needs, while continuing to hire for our ambitions toward our 2027-2030 strategy.

Recruitment is an important part of that next phase.

We are creating a dedicated Senior Talent Acquisition Partner role to take ownership of how recruitment works across Impact Fund Denmark from attraction and sourcing to assessment, candidate experience and offer.

Hiring managers make the final hiring decision. Your role is to make sure they reach it through a strong, well-run and well-informed process.

You will report to our Head of People & Culture.

What you’ll be working on

You will own end-to-end recruitment across the organisation, covering both investment roles and corporate and support functions.

For each hire, you will take the process from the first conversation with the hiring manager through to offer. You will be responsible for keeping the process moving, maintaining a high standard and making sure both candidates and hiring managers know what to expect.

At the same time, you are responsible for anchoring the recruitment process in the organisation, training hiring manager or appointed recruitment panel, and meticulous documentation of the hiring process and decisions to ensure compliance.

That includes:

• 
advising hiring managers on role definition, the candidate market and the right recruitment approach 

• 
delivering a professional and engaging candidate journey from start to finish, including a welcoming, seamless and positive on-site experience for arriving candidates 

• 
coordinating, overseeing and driving end-to-end recruitment processes in close collaboration with hiring managers 

• 
sourcing directly, mapping relevant markets and reaching out to candidates who may not be actively looking 

• 
Identifying, sourcing and vetting talents on different channels to find top-tier active and passive candidates, and conduct initial screening interviews to assess technical and interpersonal-skills as well as cultural alignment 

• 
screening and interviewing candidates and helping managers design structured, relevant assessments 

• 
managing timelines, expectations and communication from intake through to offer 

• 
briefing and managing external search or recruitment partners when we use them 

• 
setting and ensuring a consistent standard for job ads, interviews, candidate communication and hiring documentation 

• 
building talent pipelines and market knowledge for recurring or difficult-to-fill profiles 

• 
using recruitment data to improve hiring quality, timeliness and cost-effectiveness, and demonstrate responsible use of recruitment resources in a state-owned organisation 

• 
improving our recruitment tools, templates and ways of working over time 

• 
ensuring that selection criteria, candidate assessments, approvals and hiring decisions are clearly documented and traceable, supporting public-sector governance, compliance with applicable rules and internal policies, and auditability under the Danish standards on public-sector auditing (SOR) 

• 
contributing to selected People & Culture projects alongside recruitment where it makes sense 

• 
training and guiding hiring managers on recruitment processes and guidelines to drive fair, consistent hiring decisions 

We use Talentech as our applicant tracking system and CatalystOne as our HR system.

What a good first year looks like

After your first year, we would expect that:

• 
Recruitment has a clear owner. Hiring managers know where to go for advice and support, and there is a consistent professional standard across the organisation. 

• 
Processes are stronger and more consistent. Roles are well defined, assessments are structured, and recruitment decisions are properly documented. 

• 
Hiring processes keeps moving. Managers receive relevant, well-screened candidate fields, and processes keep momentum on the factors within your control. 

• 
We rely less on who happens to apply. Direct sourcing is used actively where needed, and external search partners are brought in selectively and managed closely. 

What we’re looking for

This role needs someone who is comfortable owning recruitment rather than simply coordinating it.

You will need to bring:

• 
Solid experience independently managing end-to-end recruitment 

• 
strong direct-sourcing experience, including outreach to passive candidates 

• 
experience recruiting into a professional, knowledge-intensive environment 

• 
confidence advising senior and demanding hiring managers 

• 
the ability to keep recruitment processes moving and hold people to agreed timelines 

• 
experience screening and interviewing candidates, with good judgement about assessment quality 

• 
strong structure, follow-through and attention to the documentation behind hiring decisions 

• 
professional fluency in Danish and English 

It would be useful, but is not essential, if you also have experience with one or more of the following:

• 
recruiting investment or financial-services professionals 

• 
executive search or other senior professional recruitment 

• 
briefing and managing external search or recruitment partners 

• 
market mapping, talent intelligence or proactive pipeline building 

• 
using recruitment data and metrics to improve processes 

• 
international recruitment 

Where the role sits

This is a Lead role with no direct reports. You will have full ownership of the recruitment lifecycle, meaning you should be comfortable balancing high-level strategy and manager coaching with hands-on execution, including the day-to-day administrative and coordination tasks, candidate care and operational execution.

You will be the main point of contact for recruitment across Impact Fund Denmark and the person responsible for how recruitment is run and for its quality.

Hiring managers remain accountable for who they hire. You bring the candidate market knowledge, recruitment expertise and process that help them make those decisions well.

That means being willing to challenge a brief when necessary, being realistic about the market, keeping a process moving when other priorities compete for attention, and making sure candidate experience does not become an afterthought.

For specialist searches, or during periods of particularly high hiring activity, you will also work with HRBP colleagues and external search partners. For periods of low activity you will build adjacent HR capabilities and part take in leadership development,....

Why join Impact Fund Denmark?

You will have the opportunity to shape how recruitment is done across the organisation rather than inherit a narrowly defined part of the process.

You will work closely with the Head of People & Culture and with senior leaders across the organisation, including our investment teams.

The role is unusually broad for an internal recruitment position. One search may be for an investment professional with a highly specialised background; the next may be for a corporate or functional expert.

And the work connects directly to Impact Fund Denmark's purpose. Every person you help bring into the organisation contributes, in some way, to investments in green energy and infrastructure, financial services, sustainable food systems and healthcare in developing countries.

Practical details

• 
Location: Østbanegade 135, 2100 Copenhagen Ø 

• 
Position: Permanent, full-time, 39 hours per week including lunch 

• 
Hybrid working: Up to 20% of working time from home 

• 
Application deadline: 23 September 2026

• 
Hybrid: We currently have up to 20% of working time from home starting after 6 months of employment. We believe being in office is important for successful onboarding and integration into team and organisation. 

Please apply through our talent platform. Applications submitted outside the platform will not be considered.

We review applications on an ongoing basis.

jobs.occupation: Kitchen Sous Chef – Yakitori Specialist at La Pausa Restaurant
jobs.description:
English Version Below

Køkken Souschef med speciale i Yakitori hos La Pausa Restaurant

Vi søger en dygtig og erfaren køkken souschef med speciale i japansk yakitori til vores køkken.

Du bliver en central del af køkkenteamet og får ansvar for den daglige drift af yakitori-køkkenet samt for at sikre høj kvalitet og ensartethed i tilberedning og grillning.

Dine primære arbejdsopgaver vil være:

• 
Tilberedning og tilberedningsforberedelse af yakitori

• 
Grillning af yakitori på professionelt niveau

• 
Ansvar for den daglige drift og organisering af yakitori-køkkenet

• 
Koordinering og vejledning af køkkenpersonalet

• 
Sikring af kvalitet, smag, præsentation og ensartede standarder

• 
Udvikling og design af nye yakitori-retter og menuer

• 
Bidrage til udvikling af køkkenets koncept og arbejdsgange

• 
Sikre god hygiejne, orden og effektivt serviceflow

• 
Assistere køkkenchefen og varetage dennes funktion efter behov

Vi forventer, at du:

• 
Har solid erfaring med japansk køkken og særligt yakitori

• 
Har dokumenterede færdigheder inden for yakitori-tilberedning og grillning

• 
Har erfaring med at arbejde professionelt med yakitori-grill

• 
Har forståelse for råvarer, udskæring, marinering, tilberedning og grillteknikker

• 
Har erfaring med menuudvikling og gerne udvikling af nye yakitori-koncepter

• 
Kan arbejde selvstændigt og tage ansvar for et køkkenområde

• 
Har gode samarbejds- og lederevner

• 
Kan arbejde struktureret og bevare overblikket i et travlt køkken

• 
Har fokus på kvalitet, detaljer og gæsteoplevelsen

Det er en fordel, hvis du har erfaring fra en restaurant, hvor yakitori udgør en væsentlig del af køkkenets koncept.

Vi tilbyder:

• 
En spændende stilling med ansvar og mulighed for at sætte dit præg på køkkenet

• 
Mulighed for at udvikle nye retter og menuer

• 
Et professionelt og dynamisk arbejdsmiljø

• 
Mulighed for faglig udvikling og større ansvar

Stillingen er en fuldtidsstilling. Løn og øvrige ansættelsesvilkår aftales efter kvalifikationer og erfaring.

Vi søger en souschef, som ikke blot kan tilberede yakitori, men som har et stærkt fagligt niveau inden for hele yakitori-processen og kan være med til at udvikle og drive et professionelt yakitori-køkken.

ENGLISH:

Kitchen Sous Chef – Yakitori Specialist at La Pausa Restaurant

We are looking for a skilled and experienced Kitchen Sous Chef specializing in Japanese yakitori to join our kitchen team.

You will play a key role in the daily operation of the yakitori kitchen and will be responsible for maintaining a consistently high standard of preparation, grilling, quality and presentation.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• 
Preparation and mise en place of yakitori

• 
Professional yakitori grilling

• 
Responsibility for the daily operation and organization of the yakitori kitchen

• 
Coordinating and guiding kitchen staff

• 
Ensuring consistent quality, taste, presentation and preparation standards

• 
Developing and designing new yakitori dishes and menus

• 
Contributing to the development of the kitchen concept and working procedures

• 
Maintaining high standards of hygiene, organization and service flow

• 
Assisting the Head Chef and taking responsibility in their absence when required

We expect you to:

• 
Have solid professional experience in Japanese cuisine, particularly yakitori

• 
Have proven skills in yakitori preparation and grilling

• 
Have professional experience working with a yakitori grill

• 
Have a strong understanding of ingredients, cutting techniques, marinating, preparation and grilling techniques

• 
Have experience with menu development and preferably developing new yakitori concepts

• 
Be able to work independently and take responsibility for a kitchen section

• 
Have good teamwork and leadership skills

• 
Be organized and able to maintain an overview in a busy kitchen

• 
Have a strong focus on quality, detail and the guest experience

Experience from a restaurant where yakitori is an important part of the kitchen concept will be considered an advantage.

We offer:

• 
An exciting position with responsibility and the opportunity to influence the development of the kitchen

• 
The opportunity to develop new dishes and menus

• 
A professional and dynamic working environment

• 
Opportunities for professional development and increased responsibility

This is a full-time position. Salary and employment terms will be agreed according to qualifications and experience.

We are looking for a sous chef who not only knows how to prepare yakitori, but who has a strong professional understanding of the entire yakitori process and can help develop and operate a professional yakitori kitchen.

About Thorsbjerggaard

Thorsbjerggaard is a Danish farm specializing in the cultivation of edible pumpkins. Our products are supplied to many major Danish supermarkets and specialty stores. We also grow peas, squash, and watermelons.

All work is carried out on the farm, including cultivation, harvesting, washing, and packing.

A valid forklift certificate is an advantage and will be preferred.

The certificate must be valid for use in Europe.

Working Period

As soon as possible – end of March 2027

Working Hours

During warm periods, work usually starts at 5:00 a.m. and continues until around 12:00 noon. During busy periods, additional work in the afternoon may be required.

Working hours may vary depending on the weather and workload. Part-time work may occur. You will have at least one day off per week.

Language Requirements

You must be able to speak and understand English.

Wages

Monthly salary

Registered with the Danish tax authorities (SKAT)

Salary paid directly into your bank account, with a pay slip

Requirements

• 
You must be at least 18 years old.

• 
EU citizenship (a valid passport or national ID card is required).

• 
Good physical condition, motivation, and a positive attitude.

• 
Farm or harvesting experience is an advantage but not required.

• 
A clean criminal record certificate from your home country.

We Expect You To

• 
Be reliable and arrive on time.

• 
Be flexible and willing to help wherever needed.

• 
Work well as part of a team with people from different cultures.

• 
Be able to communicate in English.

Accommodation

We have a campsite located on the farm, where you can rent a space in a caravan. Each caravan can accommodate up to four people.

Beds with mattresses are provided, but you must bring your own sleeping bag and bed linen.

The campsite offers access to toilets, showers, laundry facilities, shared cooking facilities (you prepare your own meals), and internet access.

The accommodation fee is all-inclusive.

The cost of accommodation in a caravan is DKK 70 per person per day. A refundable deposit of DKK 1,500 is required and will be returned if everything is left in the same condition as when you arrived.

Holiday Allowance

Holiday allowance will be transferred to FerieKonto and paid according to Danish holiday regulations.

Hygiene Rules

All hygiene regulations relating to the handling and harvesting of food products must be strictly followed. You will receive detailed instructions before starting work.

Failure to follow the hygiene rules may result in immediate dismissal without further warning.

What to Bring

• 
Please remember to bring:

• 
Sleeping bag

• 
Warm clothing

• 
Practical work clothes

• 
Boots and waterproof clothing

• 
Even in good weather, the plants can be very wet in the morning.

Important Documents

You must bring:

• 
A valid national ID card (and passport, if possible)

• 
A valid IBAN bank account in your own name

• 
Documentation proving that you have health insurance in your home country

• 
Tax Information 2026

• 
You must bring documentation showing that you have a permanent address in your home country.

• 
If you worked for us last year and have had other jobs since then, please bring documentation from your most recent employer.

• 
If you are married, documentation of your marital status is required.

• 
Please bring copies of all original documents, as well as English translations.

How to Apply

Please send your application and relevant documents to:

job@thorsbjerggaard.dk

If you do not hear from us within two weeks, please assume that your application was unsuccessful and that we are unable to offer you a position for 2026.

As Impact Fund Denmark continues to grow and professionalise, we want more of our people and organisational decisions to be grounded in evidence, data and a clear understanding of what drives behaviour and performance.

That is why we are creating a new role at the intersection of People Analytics, Reward and Talent.

You might already work in HR and be looking to build deeper analytical expertise. Or you may come from organisational psychology, economics, analytics or a related field and want to apply your skills in a People & Culture setting.

Either way, what matters most is that you are curious about how organisations work, comfortable working with data, and able to turn analysis into useful insights and practical recommendations and that you take pride in contributing and getting things to impact.

You will report to our Head of People & Culture.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Your role is to help us understand our organisation better — and use that understanding to make better decisions.

Your work will span analytics, reward and talent. You will:

• 
Analyse employee, performance, engagement, talent and compensation data

• 
Turn data and research into clear conclusions and practical recommendations for People & Culture and management

• 
Support compensation benchmarking and our annual salary and compensation processes

• 
Contribute to the implementation of the EU Pay Transparency requirements, including the related analysis and reporting

• 
Develop dashboards, recurring People reporting and metrics that help us focus on what matters

• 
Analyse engagement survey results and help turn them into meaningful organisational actions

• 
Support talent, succession and performance processes with analysis and insight

• 
Bring relevant research from organisational psychology and behavioural science into the way we design and evaluate People initiatives

• 
Challenge assumptions and help us understand whether our interventions are having the intended effect

• 
Prepare clear presentations and decision material for colleagues and leadership

• 
Contribute to selected organisational development and talent projects

YOUR FIRST YEAR

By the end of your first year, we would expect to see progress in five areas:

• 
Data: our People reporting and analytics are clearer, more consistent and more useful

• 
Reward: compensation processes are supported by reliable analysis and relevant market data

• 
Listening: employee survey data is translated into meaningful insights rather than simply reported

• 
Evidence: important People initiatives increasingly have a clear evidence base, purpose and intended outcome

• 
Decision support: People & Culture and leadership receive concise, relevant analysis that helps them make better decisions

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

This is what we need to see:

• 
A relevant academic background, for example in psychology, organisational psychology, economics, business, HR, statistics or another analytical discipline

• 
Strong quantitative and analytical skills

• 
A few years of relevant professional experience. We care more about the quality and relevance of your experience than an exact number of years

• 
Strong Excel skills and confidence working with data

• 
The ability to move from data or research to a clear conclusion and a practical recommendation

• 
Intellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in understanding why People practices work — rather than simply following established practice

• 
Strong written and verbal communication skills

• 
Professional fluency in English

These would be advantages, but they are not requirements:

• 
Previous HR experience

• 
Experience with Compensation & Benefits or Reward

• 
Experience with People Analytics, employee surveys or HR reporting

• 
Knowledge of statistics or research methodology

• 
Experience with Power BI or similar visualisation tools

• 
Experience applying organisational psychology or behavioural science in an organisational setting

• 
Emotional intelligence, active listening and the ability to stay neutral under pressure

• 
Courage to address uncomfortable issues, strong mediation and conflict-resolution capability

• 
Professional fluency in Danish

WHERE THE ROLE SITS

This is an individual-contributor role within People & Culture.

You will work closely with the Head of People & Culture and with colleagues responsible for People Partnering, Operations and Recruitment.

Your role is to bring analytical depth and an evidence-based perspective to the areas where it can improve our decisions — particularly Reward, Talent, engagement and organisational development.

The scope is intentionally broad enough for you to grow and develop, but the professional core is clear: using data and evidence to improve people and organisational decisions.

WHY JOIN US

This is an opportunity to:

• 
Help build a new capability at the intersection of People Analytics, Reward and Talent

• 
Work closely with the Head of People & Culture and colleagues across the function

• 
Apply data, research and behavioural science to real organisational questions

• 
Build broad experience across compensation, talent, engagement and organisational development

• 
Work in an organisation where the People agenda connects to a wider purpose: our colleagues support investments in green energy and infrastructure, financial services, sustainable food systems and healthcare in developing countries

PRACTICAL DETAILS

• 
Location: Østbanegade 135, 2100 Copenhagen Ø

• 
Position: Permanent, full-time, 39 hours per week including lunch

• 
Hybrid: We currently have up to 20% of working time from home. We aim for first 6 months of employment to be in office for successful onboarding and integration into team and organisation.

• 
Application deadline: 23 September 2026

Please apply through our talent platform. Applications submitted outside the platform will not be considered.

We review applications on an ongoing basis.

About Impact Fund Denmark

Impact Fund Denmark (IFU – the Investment Fund for Developing Countries) is a Danish impact investor contributing to green, just and inclusive societies as well as supporting the Sustainable Development Goals. Impact Fund Denmark provides risk capital to companies operating in developing countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and parts of Europe. Investments are made on commercial terms in the form of equity, loans and guarantees. Impact Fund Denmark has co-invested in over 1,300 companies in more than 100 developing countries and emerging markets. Contracted investments total EUR 31 billion, of which Impact Fund Denmark has contributed EUR 3.4 billion. Capital under management will be growing from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 5.0 billion over the next few years. Read more at Impact Fund Denmark

Styre bestillingsrutiner, lager og vareoptælling samt træde til og dække for vores Operations Manager ved behov.

Opdage flaskehalse i tide og eksekvere praktiske løsninger proaktivt.

Håndtere gæstefeedback, kundehenvendelser og daglig kommunikation.

Drive lokal forretningsudvikling, samarbejder og community-aktiveringer.

Økonomistyring & rapportering:

Følge op på det daglige salg, lønomkostninger og dækningsgrader for at identificere optimeringsmuligheder.

Klargøre ugentlige løn- og performancerapporter forud for ledelsesmøder.

Rapportere drift, bemanding og strategiske forslag løbende til ejerkredsen/bestyrelsen.

En definerende lederrolle i et af Københavns mest anerkendte pizzakoncepter.

Reelt mandat og indflydelse på virksomhedens processer, teamkultur og forretningsvækst.

En støttende og sammentømret teamkultur med høj energi og stort fokus på håndværket.

Konkurrencedygtig løn efter kvalifikationer samt personalegoder.

En fleksibel arbejdsplan.

General Manager — Diamond Slice, Copenhagen (Nørrebro)

Do you thrive in high-energy hospitality, love sourdough pizza made at the highest level, and bring the operational backbone to run a fast-growing restaurant brand?

Since opening on Blågårds Plads, Diamond Slice has redefined New York-style pizza in Copenhagen. With two bustling neighborhood shops in Nørrebro (Blågårds Plads and Tagensvej 79), an expanding catering wing, and a major footprint at Roskilde Festival and summer events, we are looking for a sharp, driven General Manager.

As General Manager, you will lead the business side of Diamond Slice. Working in close partnership with our Operations Manager and team leaders, you will establish solid systems, drive FOH performance, and ensure our shops run smoothly, efficiently, and autonomously.

Key Focus Areas & Responsibilities

Business Operations & Systems:

• 
Drive day-to-day business operations across locations alongside the Operations Manager.

• 
Build, streamline, and maintain dependable daily routines, systems, and team accountability.

Oversee ordering schedules, inventory, and stock control; step in to cover for the Operations Manager when needed.

Spot bottlenecks early and execute practical solutions proactively.

•

•

Handle guest feedback, inquiries, and daily customer communications.

Catering, Festivals & Growth:

• 
Coordinate incoming catering requests and event logistics with the Operations Manager and event team.

• 
Take operational ownership of Diamond Slice’s festival setups (including Roskilde Festival), including volunteers, staff, and logistics.

• 
Drive local business development, collaborations, and community activations.

• 
Financial Control & Reporting:

• 
Monitor daily sales, labor costs, and operational margins to identify efficiency gains.

• 
Prepare weekly labor and performance summaries for leadership meetings.

• 
Report regularly on operations, staffing, and strategic proposals to the ownership group/board.

What We Are Looking For

• 
Proven Track Record: 2+ years of management experience in high-tempo hospitality (e.g., General Manager, Assistant GM, or Operations Manager).

• 
Systems & Numbers: Experience managing scheduling tools, POS/inventory setups, and keeping labor percentages on budget.

• 
Hands-on Leadership: You lead by example during rushes, bring calm energy under pressure, and set high hospitality standards.

• 
Languages: Professional working proficiency in English is required (international team). Conversational or fluent Danish is a strong advantage for local administration and supplier coordination.

What We Offer

A defining leadership role in one of Copenhagen’s most celebrated pizza concepts.

• 
Real autonomy and influence over company processes, team culture, and business growth.

• 
A supportive, close-knit team culture with great energy and high craftsmanship.

Competitive salary matching qualifications, and company perks.

A flexible schedule.

jobs.occupation: Part-time Administrative Officer for the Centre for Industrial Mechanics
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a part-time Administrative Officer position at the Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the SDU Sønderborg campus.

We are looking for a structured and proactive colleague who can support the Centre’s day-to-day administration, assist with project coordination, and contribute to the planning and organization of conferences, workshops, meetings and other academic and industrial events. The position offers the opportunity to work in an international university environment with close interaction with academic staff, students, external partners and administrative units.

Unique opportunity

The Centre for Industrial Mechanics combines research, education and collaboration with industry across areas including mechanical engineering, energy systems, renewable energy, artificial intelligence, mechatronics and related technologies. As the Centre continues to develop its activities and external collaborations, effective administrative and project support is important for ensuring smooth daily operations and successful delivery of events and projects.

The successful candidate will become part of an international and collaborative working environment and will have a varied portfolio of tasks. The role is well suited to a person who enjoys organizing, coordinating and communicating, and who is comfortable handling both routine administrative duties and changing priorities.

Workplace description

The Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at SDU conducts research and education from fundamental engineering principles to applied solutions. The Centre for Industrial Mechanics is located in the Alsion building at SDU’s Sønderborg campus and benefits from strong connections with companies and organizations in Southern Denmark and Northern Germany. The working environment is international, and English is widely used in daily communication.

Duties of the position

• 
Conference and Event Organization: Support the planning and practical organization of conferences, workshops, seminars, project meetings and other events. Tasks may include registration, participant communication, invitations, agendas, room coordination, catering, travel arrangements, accommodation, event materials and on-site support.

• 
Daily Administrative Support: Assist with general administrative tasks for the Centre and its research groups, including correspondence, document preparation, meeting coordination, scheduling, filing, maintaining administrative records and following up on agreed actions.

• 
Project Administration and Coordination: Support externally and internally funded projects with practical project-management tasks such as meeting planning, collection of inputs from partners, follow-up on deadlines and deliverables, preparation of simple status overviews, and coordination of project documentation.

• 
Meeting Support: Organize internal and external meetings, prepare agendas and supporting material when required, take meeting notes or minutes, and assist with follow-up of decisions and action points.

• 
Communication and Stakeholder Coordination: Communicate professionally with colleagues, students, project partners, companies, conference participants and other external stakeholders, and help ensure that relevant information is shared in a timely and structured manner.

• 
Travel and Visit Coordination: Assist with practical arrangements for staff travel, guest visits, invited speakers and visiting researchers in accordance with SDU procedures.

• 
Documentation and Information Management: Maintain structured project and administrative files, contact lists, event information, templates, presentations and other shared material, and support the collection and organization of information needed for reports and internal follow-up.

• 
Financial and Procurement Support: Provide practical administrative assistance related to purchases, invoices, reimbursements, budgets and project expenses in coordination with the relevant SDU administrative functions. The role does not require responsibility for formal financial approval.

• 
Other Administrative Tasks: Contribute flexibly to other administrative and organizational tasks that arise in the daily operation of the Centre and its projects.

We are seeking a reliable and motivated candidate with strong organizational and communication skills. The position does not require a specific advanced academic specialization; a relevant Bachelor’s or Master’s degree is sufficient.

• 
A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in business administration, management, communication, social sciences, humanities, engineering management, public administration, project management, or another relevant field.

• 
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage several tasks, deadlines and stakeholders in parallel.

• 
Good written and verbal communication skills in English.

• 
A structured, responsible and service-oriented approach to administrative work.

•
